content.text:
I read every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, and built a full ledger tracing each claim limitation, numeral, and figure statement to an affirmative inventor passage.

**What I traced (representative):**

- **Claims 1–20** — rigid base with first/second sides, motor on the first side, air-extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction loop/skirt (plastic, metal, PTFE, combinations), non-sealing perimeter admitting air, continuous extraction holding the chamber below atmospheric, hands-free holding force, rigid all-rigid vibration path, sliding while held, handle for guiding, rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled control — all map to explicit sentences in `input/disclosure.md`. Claim 10 and the FIG. 6 embodiment map to the one affirmative USER passage adding autonomous mode ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion").
- **Numerals 10–48** — every entry is defined once, used with one meaning in the description, and appears on at least one sheet; no numeral is labeled on a sheet without being recited in that figure's Brief Description sentence.
- **Section lines** — "2-2" and "4-4" carry the same designation in the FIG. 3 source-view brief, the FIG. 2/FIG. 4 view lines, and the Brief Description of the Drawings.
- **Depiction conventions** — the rectangular slab/ring/blocks, the FIG. 2 through-base gap, the flat lower end in FIG. 4, and the FIG. 6 block placement are each disclaimed inside their briefs, verbalize no taper, angle, depth ordering, circumferential position, or contact topology beyond what the disclosure states, and are not echoed into the application text as "by way of example" or as a broadened embodiment.

No drafting note, placeholder, question, instruction, or unresolved alternative remains in any filed section, and I found no claim/description term or relationship mismatch.

input.summary: Full source ledger built and closed with no unsupported matter. I checked every claim limitation in claims 1-20, every numeral and numbered part in draft/numerals.md (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48), all six figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings, and traced each item to an affirmative inventor passage in input/disclosure.md or to the single affirmative USER passage in input/conversation.md. Representative traces: rigid base with a first side carrying the vibration motor and a second side carrying the chamber, and the air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side in fluid communication with that chamber ("a vibration motor coupled to a first side of a rigid base. An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base"); the rigid low-friction perimeter member, its material list (plastic, metal, PTFE, combinations of rigid materials), and its non-sealing behavior ("formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials"; "not intended to form a complete airtight seal and does not rely on flexible rubber or foam. Instead, it restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile"); the clearance along at least part of the member and the continuous inflow of ambient air ("continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter, maintaining the chamber at a lower pressure than the surrounding atmosphere"); hands-free holding force ("holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward"); the all-rigid vibration transmission path with no elastomeric, foam or resilient member ("the vibration motor is connected to the tile through rigid components, vibration energy is transferred with substantially less damping"); simultaneous holding and sliding ("the low-friction perimeter allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact"); the guiding handle ("one or more handles used primarily for guiding the machine rather than pressing it"); the rope/wire/cable pulling element and decoupled control ("Pulling the flexible element moves the device across the tile, while the pressure differential independently supplies the force holding the device against the surface"); and claim 10, the summary paragraph and the FIG. 6 embodiment, traced to the one affirmative USER passage adding autonomous mode ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"). Operational USER turns (resume, revalidate, tighten the Field, publish only when gates pass) were treated as context and relied on for no technical matter, and prior-art characterizations in the Background were not required to have inventor support. Internal consistency verified: each numeral has one meaning across claims, description, ledger and briefs; every numeral labeled on a sheet is recited in that sheet's Brief Description sentence; section designations 2-2 and 4-4 repeat identically in the FIG. 3 source-view brief, the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 view lines, and draft/07; the FIG. 2 Brief Description enumeration (base, chamber, perimeter member, covering element in section; air-extraction mechanism in elevation; motor and handle omitted) matches the FIG. 2 brief's cut bodies; FIG. 6's "not separately shown" recital matches the single-block brief; and no drafting note, placeholder, question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any filed section. Depiction conventions were tested against the functional-surface rule: the rectangular slab, ring and blocks, the FIG. 2 through-base gap, the flat lower end of the column in FIG. 4 and the FIG. 6 block placement are each disclaimed inside their own briefs, rest on affirmatively disclosed parts (fluid communication, bearing contact, stirring elements), verbalize no taper, angle, runout, depth ordering, circumferential position or contact topology beyond the sources, and are not echoed into the application text as "by way of example", "any closed outline" or any added optional embodiment. Claims, description, abstract and Field remain shape-neutral and location-neutral, so no convention leaks out of the figure briefs.
